findings.text: the cause narrative says the base test's own guard refused the copy before the reload under test could run, but neither logged base run nor my re-run ever reaches that guard: both fail earlier at the raced first read (the base file's line 113, _queue.Empty, nine lines before the guard at line 122), and the record's own reproduction paragraph at :567-569 reports that same _queue.Empty — so the guard refusal is a static prediction presented as the observed failure, and a reader reproducing it will meet a timeout instead; the Measure sentence at :572-574 ("1 failed, 8 passed at 2848d3c9") likewise assigns the base test file's red to the repaired id, which cannot redden there because the product is unchanged.

"every log header naming the revision, tree, command and imported recovery.__file__" is true of one of the nine logs: five carry no header at all — including final-head-483b2839.log, the only record of the gate result — and two of the four headers that exist name revision, tree and command without the module path, so the gate's provenance lives in the manifest rather than in the artifact it cites.

_await_attached returns the first queued line without checking that it is a probe row and without draining rows rendered in the same follower tick; with the follower polling at 0.1s (reckon/cli.py:1912) against this 1.0s read, a follower stall past about 0.9s leaves a second probe row queued for the first measured read, which then fails rendered_nodes == expected_nodes (:181) with a message about node coverage rather than about the probe leak — read until the measured node set is complete, discarding probe rows, to close the window.
